title: Rewriting SupportMail's sharding system
excerpt: Replaced SupportMail's Bun-based sharding library with a Go supervisor for zero-downtime deploys and working error tracking.
content_html:
SupportMail is a Discord bot - modmail to be specific - managing so many users that it can't live in a single gateway connection anymore. Like every bot at that size, it has to shard: split its servers across multiple connections and, past a certain point, multiple processes. For a long time that machinery was a standalone Node/Bun scaling library, spawning and managing cluster child processes around the bot. Over the last few weeks I replaced it with a purpose-built supervisor written in Go, a rewritten cluster harness, and a proper split between the bot's REST API and the bot itself.

This post is about that rewrite: why the old setup wasn't ideal, what I built instead, and what's actually better now.

Note: the term developers use for "Discord servers" is "guild".

What sharding actually is, and what SupportMail had before

If you're not deep in Discord bot internals, "sharding" is a word you've probably heard without ever needing to know what it means. Worth explaining, since the rest of this post leans on it.

A shard is one gateway connection to Discord, responsible for a subset of guilds. Discord doesn't let you put every guild your bot is in on a single WebSocket connection - past a certain size, one connection can't keep up with the event volume, and Discord enforces this by requiring you to shard once your bot crosses a guild-count threshold. Which guild belongs to which shard isn't arbitrary: it's (guildId >> 22) % totalShards, a deterministic hash so any part of the system can figure out, without asking anyone, which shard owns a given guild.

That's the easy part. The harder part is that "more shards" isn't free - you can't just open five hundred gateway connections from one process and call it done. Shards get grouped into clusters, where each cluster is a separate process holding a handful of shards. And the moment you have multiple processes, you need something above them deciding how many clusters to run, which shards go in which cluster, restarting a cluster that dies, and giving the outside world (an API, a dashboard) a single place to ask "is guild X's shard even alive right now." That something is a supervisor.

SupportMail's old supervisor was galactic.ts, a sharding manager from another bot, using node's child_process module. My fork of it used Bun.spawn() to fork cluster child processes from a StandaloneInstance, all living inside the same Bun process that also ran the bot's REST API on port 3000 and a WebSocket server on port 4000. Everything - gateway connections, HTTP, sockets, the supervisor logic itself - was one Bun process tree.

If "why shard" didn't land, the next few sections won't either - splitting structural ops from business ops, generation-based deploys, same idea. Still just multiple processes and one coordinator, only smaller.

Why replace it instead of patching it

The concrete pain that started this whole rewrite: Bun.spawn, child_process, and worker threads used from inside the bot process broke Sentry instrumentation. The main process was still Bun. Errors events published over node's diagnostics_channel simply didn't work and were silently lost the moment cluster children got involved. This was a "I can't trust my own error reporting" bug.

That alone was not really patchable since Bun's release schedule is weird and the open PR didn't seem to be merged soon - the latest Bun release was also over two months ago and there were no signs of a new release. What made it not worth patching was what sat underneath it: galactic.ts's Instance/Cluster classes are coupled to the assumption that the parent process is Bun. The choice was patch it in place and stay Bun-native, or drop it entirely and go external in a different language. Nothing in between. And once you look past galactic.ts itself, most of what it managed wasn't hard to begin with: discord.js already supports multiple shards in one process natively (internal sharding) — galactic.ts handled orchestration around that, not the sharding itself.

To be fair to the old code - the reclustering-without-downtime logic, the IPC communication between processes and the cleanup I added in my fork weren't dead weight. They were useful reference material for the generation/quiesce handoff I ended up building - parts worth keeping got kept as reference, parts that were structurally unsuitable got replaced.

Alternatives considered

The section above covers why patching galactic.ts in place was off the table. Even setting that aside, staying in-process wasn't the right call: SupportMail isn't the only bot I run - I also have Ticketon, which might need the same infrastructure someday - and a manager wired into one bot's process can't be reused without another rewrite. That's what settled it on an external, bot-agnostic supervisor in a different language.

Speaking of language, this was still open. I initially considered Rust, mainly because I wanted an excuse to learn it more. However I went with Go instead, for two reasons:

  1. The concurrency model fits the problem shape directly. "Supervise N cluster processes and fan-in their IPC over a socket" is almost exactly what goroutines and channels are for. Rust's async story - picking a runtime, Pin, Send/Sync bounds threading through everything which introduces complexity to solve a problem that Go solves with a few lines of code.
  2. Speed of building. Go's standard library (net, exec, net/http) was enough to build the supervisor, the IPC hub and the status WebSocket with almost no third-party dependencies. Rust would've meant choosing and learning an async runtime and picking up crates before writing any of the actual supervisor logic.

This doesn't mean Rust is worse. It's a "shipping-goal vs learning-goal" calculation, and for infrastructure this close to being production-critical, shipping won.

The core design decision: structural ops vs. business ops

This is the core routing design.

The manager (sm-manager) only understands five operations: REGISTER, HEARTBEAT, QUIESCE, QUIESCED, and DEPLOY. These are structural - they're about process lifecycle, not about what the bot does. Everything else that flows through the manager is an opaque string, addressed by a target, that the manager routes to the right cluster without ever looking inside it.

Why this matters: the manager never parses a business payload. It doesn't know what a "close ticket" op looks like, or a "sync guild config" op, or anything else the bot cares about - it just knows where to send it. That means the manager stays completely bot-agnostic. Having a second bot use the same infrastructure, just by using a different config file means we don't have to fork the manager codebase. (Concretely, this is the thing that would let Ticketon share sm-manager down the line, without the manager needing to know Ticketon exists.)

The alternative - a manager that understands every op - was on the table implicitly, since that's basically what a monolithic supervisor looks like. It's more coupled: every new bot feature/feature change that needs cross-cluster coordination means a manager code change, and the manager is permanently one-bot-only in practice even if nothing stops you from bolting on a second bot in theory.

Roughly, the routing looks like this:

client → sm-manager:
  { op: "DEPLOY", ... }         → structural, manager handles directly
  { op: "guild.sync", target: clusterId, payload: <opaque> }
                                → business, manager forwards untouched to target

The manager branches on whether op is one of the five structural codes. If yes, it acts. If no, it looks at the target, finds the owning cluster connection, and forwards the whole message payload.

The topology diagram below shows everything in context, including the manager, the clusters, the bot, and the API.

One terminology note: the transport under all of this is a Unix domain socket, not TCP. Go listens with net.Listen("unix", ...); the Bun-side consumers (the API and the cluster harness) connect to the same socket path with Bun.listen/Bun.connect. I still call this "IPC" throughout - IPC means inter-process communication, and a Unix socket is one mechanism for that, in the same family as pipes or shared memory.

Zero-downtime deploys: generations

The old deploy path used PM2, and PM2's restart (not reload) meant the whole bot process - manager included - went down and came back up. That's a real "gap" in gateway connections on every deploy. The naive fix, a plain reload instead of a restart, has its own failure mode: for a moment you'd have old and new code both attached and both handling the same events, i.e. duplicate event handling.

The fix I came up with is generation-tagged shard ranges. Each deploy spins up a new "generation" of clusters holding the same shard ranges as the old generation, in parallel. The manager waits for the new generation to report ready before it flips routing over to it. Only after the flip happens does it tell the old generation to quiesce - stop accepting new work, finish in flight, then exit.

The ordering is the whole point: routing flips between "new generation ready" and "old generation quiesced", never before the new one's ready (the event listeners might not be loaded, DB connection might be missing, etc.) and never long after the old one's quiesced (you'd have a gap). That ordering guarantees there's no window where a guild's events could route to two generations at once, and no window where they route to none.

I considered simpler options - a full restart, or just accepting the old downtime (even though it was just a few seconds) - and rejected them because at SupportMail's scale, a full-restart gap means dropped gateway events across every guild simultaneously, not a cosmetic blip. Rolling per-cluster deploys with a bounded quiesce window costs more implementation complexity but limits the actual "damage" to something measurable and small.

What's better now: deploys roll out cluster-by-cluster instead of all-at-once, the quiesce gap is bounded and observable instead of open-ended, and there's no duplicate-event-handling window to worry about - versus the old world, where a deploy was closer to "hope nothing important happens in that gap."

Splitting the HTTP API out

The old client-api depended directly on bot internals and lived attached to the manager process - deploying the API meant touching the same process tree as the bot.

I decided to outsource it as well - sm-api fixes that by talking to sm-manager over the exact same Unix socket protocol any other client uses - there's no special access path, no shortcut through bot internals. It's just another IPC client.

The payoff is that sm-api redeploys independently of the bot. And because it goes through the same structural/business op split described above, it never ends up back in a position where it depends on bot-internal shapes. But the fact that it's decoupled from the bot process is also a benefit.

Observability as a proof point

One more place the structural/business split paid off in practice: the public statuspage WebSocket lives on sm-manager, not on the bot. Heartbeat payloads get forwarded to it essentially verbatim, opaque to the manager the same way any other business payload is.

This confirms the split holds up outside the cases it was designed for - the manager didn't need special-casing to support a public status feed, because "forward an opaque payload without understanding it" was already the default behavior.

What's better now

  • Sentry instrumentation works - the original reason this rewrite started.
  • Deploys are near-zero-downtime, with a quiesce window that's bounded and measurable instead of "however long a restart takes."
  • The manager is bot-agnostic: a second bot is a config addition, not a manager fork.
  • The API is fully decoupled from the bot process - no shared process tree, no internal-shape dependency.
  • It's in production - SupportMail's been running on this since the cutover. Not the headline, but memory usage dropped roughly 40% after the switch.
  • Both the manager and the API are systemd services now instead of pm2-managed, so they come back automatically on a host restart without needing a process manager babysitting them.

Closing

A few things are deliberately still deferred. The transport is a Unix socket, not TCP or WebSocket, which is fine for now since everything runs on one host - but it's a constraint if that ever changes. The manager also has no high-availability story yet; it's a single process, and if it dies, it's systemd restarting it, not a hot standby taking over. Neither of these is a problem today, and neither needed solving on day one just because it's theoretically a gap. It was genuinely hard for me to find the line beteen "but what if" and "is it really needed now".

sm-manager may end up open-source at some point, since it's bot-agnostic and not SupportMail-specific. I can't give a date - I will update this post and make a separate new post when that happens.

Have good day, and if you're a Discord bot developer, I hope this post helps you think about sharding and process orchestration in a new way.

PS: Huge thanks for galactic.ts also for saving my ass during the incident I talked about in the previous post. It was a game changer and is one of the best sharding solutions for most people.

sentences.en: And the moment you have multiple processes, you need something above them deciding how many clusters to run, which shards go in which cluster, restarting a cluster that dies, and giving the outside world (an API, a dashboard) a single place to ask "is guild X's shard even alive right now."
sentences.zh: 当你有多个进程时，你需要在它们之上的东西来决定要运行多少个集群，哪些分片进入哪个集群，重新启动一个死亡的集群，并为外部世界（API，仪表板）提供一个地方来询问“公会 X 的分片现在是否还活着”。

sentences.en: That something is a supervisor.
sentences.zh: 那东西就是主管。

blocks.html_en: SupportMail's old supervisor was galactic.ts, a sharding manager from another bot, using node's child_process module. My fork of it used Bun.spawn() to fork cluster child processes from a StandaloneInstance, all living inside the same Bun process that also ran the bot's REST API on port 3000 and a WebSocket server on port 4000. Everything - gateway connections, HTTP, sockets, the supervisor logic itself - was one Bun process tree.

sentences.en: SupportMail's old supervisor was galactic.ts, a sharding manager from another bot, using node's child_process module.
sentences.zh: SupportMail 的旧主管是 gactic.ts，它是另一个机器人的分片管理器，使用节点的 child_process 模块。

sentences.en: My fork of it used Bun.spawn() to fork cluster child processes from a StandaloneInstance, all living inside the same Bun process that also ran the bot's REST API on port 3000 and a WebSocket server on port 4000.
sentences.zh: 我的它的分支使用 Bun.spawn() 从 StandaloneInstance 中分支出集群子进程，所有子进程都位于同一个 Bun 进程中，该进程还在端口 3000 上运行机器人的 REST API，并在端口 4000 上运行 WebSocket 服务器。

sentences.en: Everything - gateway connections, HTTP, sockets, the supervisor logic itself - was one Bun process tree.
sentences.zh: 一切——网关连接、HTTP、套接字、管理程序逻辑本身——都是一棵 Bun 进程树。

blocks.html_en: If "why shard" didn't land, the next few sections won't either - splitting structural ops from business ops, generation-based deploys, same idea. Still just multiple processes and one coordinator, only smaller.

sentences.en: If "why shard" didn't land, the next few sections won't either - splitting structural ops from business ops, generation-based deploys, same idea.
sentences.zh: 如果“为什么分片”没有落地，那么接下来的几个部分也不会落地 - 将结构操作与业务操作分开，基于代的部署，同样的想法。

sentences.en: Still just multiple processes and one coordinator, only smaller.
sentences.zh: 仍然只有多个进程和一个协调器，只是规模较小。

blocks.html_en: Why replace it instead of patching it

sentences.en: Why replace it instead of patching it
sentences.zh: 为什么要替换它而不是修补它

blocks.html_en: The concrete pain that started this whole rewrite: Bun.spawn, child_process, and worker threads used from inside the bot process broke Sentry instrumentation. The main process was still Bun. Errors events published over node's diagnostics_channel simply didn't work and were silently lost the moment cluster children got involved. This was a "I can't trust my own error reporting" bug.

sentences.en: The concrete pain that started this whole rewrite: Bun.spawn, child_process, and worker threads used from inside the bot process broke Sentry instrumentation.
sentences.zh: 开始整个重写的具体痛苦是：Bun.spawn、child_process 和机器人进程内部使用的工作线程破坏了 Sentry 检测。

sentences.en: The main process was still Bun.
sentences.zh: 主要工序还是包子。

sentences.en: Errors events published over node's diagnostics_channel simply didn't work and were silently lost the moment cluster children got involved.
sentences.zh: 通过节点的diagnostics_channel发布的错误事件根本不起作用，并且在集群子节点参与时就默默地丢失了。

sentences.en: This was a "I can't trust my own error reporting" bug.
sentences.zh: 这是一个“我不能相信我自己的错误报告”错误。

blocks.html_en: That alone was not really patchable since Bun's release schedule is weird and the open PR didn't seem to be merged soon - the latest Bun release was also over two months ago and there were no signs of a new release. What made it not worth patching was what sat underneath it: galactic.ts's Instance/Cluster classes are coupled to the assumption that the parent process is Bun. The choice was patch it in place and stay Bun-native, or drop it entirely and go external in a different language. Nothing in between. And once you look past galactic.ts itself, most of what it managed wasn't hard to begin with: discord.js already supports multiple shards in one process natively (internal sharding) — galactic.ts handled orchestration around that, not the sharding itself.

sentences.en: That alone was not really patchable since Bun's release schedule is weird and the open PR didn't seem to be merged soon - the latest Bun release was also over two months ago and there were no signs of a new release.
sentences.zh: 仅此一点并不能真正修补，因为 Bun 的发布时间表很奇怪，而且开放 PR 似乎并没有很快合并 - 最新的 Bun 版本也是两个多月前发布的，并且没有新版本发布的迹象。

sentences.en: What made it not worth patching was what sat underneath it: galactic.ts's Instance/Cluster classes are coupled to the assumption that the parent process is Bun.
sentences.zh: 让它不值得修补的是它下面的东西：gactic.ts 的 Instance/Cluster 类与父进程是 Bun 的假设相耦合。

sentences.en: The choice was patch it in place and stay Bun-native, or drop it entirely and go external in a different language.
sentences.zh: 选择是将其修补到位并保持 Bun 本地化，或者完全放弃它并以不同的语言进行外部处理。

sentences.en: Nothing in between.
sentences.zh: 两者之间没有什么。

sentences.en: And once you look past galactic.ts itself, most of what it managed wasn't hard to begin with: discord.js already supports multiple shards in one process natively (internal sharding) — galactic.ts handled orchestration around that, not the sharding itself.
sentences.zh: 一旦你回顾了 gactic.ts 本身，它所管理的大部分内容一开始就不难理解：discord.js 已经原生支持一个进程中的多个分片（内部分片）——gactic.ts 处理的是围绕它的编排，而不是分片本身。

blocks.html_en: To be fair to the old code - the reclustering-without-downtime logic, the IPC communication between processes and the cleanup I added in my fork weren't dead weight. They were useful reference material for the generation/quiesce handoff I ended up building - parts worth keeping got kept as reference, parts that were structurally unsuitable got replaced.

sentences.en: To be fair to the old code - the reclustering-without-downtime logic, the IPC communication between processes and the cleanup I added in my fork weren't dead weight.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，旧代码 - 无需停机的重新集群逻辑、进程之间的 IPC 通信以及我在 fork 中添加的清理并不是自重。

sentences.en: They were useful reference material for the generation/quiesce handoff I ended up building - parts worth keeping got kept as reference, parts that were structurally unsuitable got replaced.
sentences.zh: 它们对于我最终构建的生成/静止切换来说是有用的参考材料——值得保留的部件被保留作为参考，结构上不合适的部件被替换。

blocks.html_en: Alternatives considered

sentences.en: Alternatives considered
sentences.zh: 考虑的替代方案

blocks.html_en: The section above covers why patching galactic.ts in place was off the table. Even setting that aside, staying in-process wasn't the right call: SupportMail isn't the only bot I run - I also have Ticketon, which might need the same infrastructure someday - and a manager wired into one bot's process can't be reused without another rewrite. That's what settled it on an external, bot-agnostic supervisor in a different language.

sentences.en: The section above covers why patching galactic.ts in place was off the table.
sentences.zh: 上面的部分介绍了为什么无法在适当的位置修补 gactic.ts。

sentences.en: Even setting that aside, staying in-process wasn't the right call: SupportMail isn't the only bot I run - I also have Ticketon, which might need the same infrastructure someday - and a manager wired into one bot's process can't be reused without another rewrite.
sentences.zh: 即使抛开这一点，留在进程中也不是正确的选择：SupportMail 不是我运行的唯一机器人 - 我还有 Ticketon，有一天它可能需要相同的基础设施 - 并且连接到一个机器人进程的管理器如果不进行另一次重写就无法重复使用。

sentences.en: That's what settled it on an external, bot-agnostic supervisor in a different language.
sentences.zh: 这就是由外部的、与机器人无关的主管以不同的语言解决的问题。

blocks.html_en: Speaking of language, this was still open. I initially considered Rust, mainly because I wanted an excuse to learn it more. However I went with Go instead, for two reasons:

sentences.en: Speaking of language, this was still open.
sentences.zh: 说到语言，这仍然是开放的。

sentences.en: I initially considered Rust, mainly because I wanted an excuse to learn it more.
sentences.zh: 我最初考虑 Rust，主要是因为我想要一个借口来更多地了解它。

sentences.en: However I went with Go instead, for two reasons:
sentences.zh: 然而我选择了 Go，原因有两个：

blocks.html_en: • The concurrency model fits the problem shape directly. "Supervise N cluster processes and fan-in their IPC over a socket" is almost exactly what goroutines and channels are for. Rust's async story - picking a runtime, Pin, Send/Sync bounds threading through everything which introduces complexity to solve a problem that Go solves with a few lines of code.

sentences.en: The concurrency model fits the problem shape directly.
sentences.zh: 并发模型直接适合问题的形状。

sentences.en: "Supervise N cluster processes and fan-in their IPC over a socket" is almost exactly what goroutines and channels are for.
sentences.zh: “监督 N 个集群进程并通过套接字扇入它们的 IPC”几乎正是 goroutine 和通道的用途。

sentences.en: Rust's async story - picking a runtime, Pin, Send/Sync bounds threading through everything which introduces complexity to solve a problem that Go solves with a few lines of code.
sentences.zh: Rust 的异步故事 - 选择运行时、Pin、发送/同步边界线程贯穿所有内容，这会带来复杂性来解决 Go 用几行代码即可解决的问题。

blocks.html_en: • Speed of building. Go's standard library (net, exec, net/http) was enough to build the supervisor, the IPC hub and the status WebSocket with almost no third-party dependencies. Rust would've meant choosing and learning an async runtime and picking up crates before writing any of the actual supervisor logic.

sentences.en: Speed of building.
sentences.zh: 建设速度。

sentences.en: Go's standard library (net, exec, net/http) was enough to build the supervisor, the IPC hub and the status WebSocket with almost no third-party dependencies.
sentences.zh: Go 的标准库（net、exec、net/http）足以构建管理器、IPC 集线器和状态 WebSocket，几乎没有第三方依赖项。

sentences.en: Rust would've meant choosing and learning an async runtime and picking up crates before writing any of the actual supervisor logic.
sentences.zh: Rust 意味着选择和学习异步运行时，并在编写任何实际的主管逻辑之前拿起箱子。

blocks.html_en: This doesn't mean Rust is worse. It's a "shipping-goal vs learning-goal" calculation, and for infrastructure this close to being production-critical, shipping won.

sentences.en: This doesn't mean Rust is worse.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着 Rust 更糟糕。

sentences.en: It's a "shipping-goal vs learning-goal" calculation, and for infrastructure this close to being production-critical, shipping won.
sentences.zh: 这是一个“运输目标与学习目标”的计算，对于如此接近生产关键的基础设施，运输获胜。

blocks.html_en: The core design decision: structural ops vs. business ops

sentences.en: The core design decision: structural ops vs. business ops
sentences.zh: 核心设计决策：结构操作与业务操作

blocks.html_en: This is the core routing design.

sentences.en: This is the core routing design.
sentences.zh: 这就是核心路由设计。

blocks.html_en: The manager (sm-manager) only understands five operations: REGISTER, HEARTBEAT, QUIESCE, QUIESCED, and DEPLOY. These are structural - they're about process lifecycle, not about what the bot does. Everything else that flows through the manager is an opaque string, addressed by a target, that the manager routes to the right cluster without ever looking inside it.

sentences.en: The manager (sm-manager) only understands five operations: REGISTER, HEARTBEAT, QUIESCE, QUIESCED, and DEPLOY.
sentences.zh: 管理器（sm-manager）仅理解五种操作：REGISTER、HEARTBEAT、QUIESCE、QUIESCED 和 DEPLOY。

sentences.en: These are structural - they're about process lifecycle, not about what the bot does.
sentences.zh: 这些是结构性的 - 它们与流程生命周期有关，而不是与机器人的行为有关。

sentences.en: Everything else that flows through the manager is an opaque string, addressed by a target, that the manager routes to the right cluster without ever looking inside it.
sentences.zh: 流经管理器的其他所有内容都是不透明的字符串，由目标寻址，管理器将其路由到正确的集群，而无需查看其内部。

blocks.html_en: Why this matters: the manager never parses a business payload. It doesn't know what a "close ticket" op looks like, or a "sync guild config" op, or anything else the bot cares about - it just knows where to send it. That means the manager stays completely bot-agnostic. Having a second bot use the same infrastructure, just by using a different config file means we don't have to fork the manager codebase. (Concretely, this is the thing that would let Ticketon share sm-manager down the line, without the manager needing to know Ticketon exists.)

sentences.en: Why this matters: the manager never parses a business payload.
sentences.zh: 为什么这很重要：管理器从不解析业务负载。

sentences.en: It doesn't know what a "close ticket" op looks like, or a "sync guild config" op, or anything else the bot cares about - it just knows where to send it.
sentences.zh: 它不知道“关闭票证”操作是什么样子，或者“同步行会配置”操作，或者机器人关心的任何其他东西 - 它只知道将其发送到哪里。

sentences.en: That means the manager stays completely bot-agnostic.
sentences.zh: 这意味着经理完全与机器人无关。

sentences.en: Having a second bot use the same infrastructure, just by using a different config file means we don't have to fork the manager codebase.
sentences.zh: 让第二个机器人使用相同的基础设施，只需使用不同的配置文件就意味着我们不必分叉管理器代码库。

sentences.en: (Concretely, this is the thing that would let Ticketon share sm-manager down the line, without the manager needing to know Ticketon exists.)
sentences.zh: （具体来说，这可以让 Ticketon 共享 sm-manager，而经理无需知道 Ticketon 的存在。）

blocks.html_en: The alternative - a manager that understands every op - was on the table implicitly, since that's basically what a monolithic supervisor looks like. It's more coupled: every new bot feature/feature change that needs cross-cluster coordination means a manager code change, and the manager is permanently one-bot-only in practice even if nothing stops you from bolting on a second bot in theory.

sentences.en: The alternative - a manager that understands every op - was on the table implicitly, since that's basically what a monolithic supervisor looks like.
sentences.zh: 另一种选择——一个理解每项操作的管理者——已经隐式地摆在了桌面上，因为这基本上就是单一主管的样子。

sentences.en: It's more coupled: every new bot feature/feature change that needs cross-cluster coordination means a manager code change, and the manager is permanently one-bot-only in practice even if nothing stops you from bolting on a second bot in theory.
sentences.zh: 它的耦合性更强：每一个需要跨集群协调的新机器人功能/功能更改都意味着管理器代码更改，并且管理器在实践中永远只有一个机器人，即使理论上没有什么可以阻止您转向第二个机器人。

blocks.html_en: Roughly, the routing looks like this:

sentences.en: Roughly, the routing looks like this:
sentences.zh: 粗略地说，路由看起来像这样：

blocks.html_en: The manager branches on whether op is one of the five structural codes. If yes, it acts. If no, it looks at the target, finds the owning cluster connection, and forwards the whole message payload.

sentences.en: The manager branches on whether op is one of the five structural codes.
sentences.zh: 管理器根据 op 是否是五个结构代码之一进行分支。

sentences.en: If yes, it acts.
sentences.zh: 如果是，它就会起作用。

sentences.en: If no, it looks at the target, finds the owning cluster connection, and forwards the whole message payload.
sentences.zh: 如果不是，它会查看目标，找到所属的集群连接，然后转发整个消息负载。

blocks.html_en: One terminology note: the transport under all of this is a Unix domain socket, not TCP. Go listens with net.Listen("unix", ...); the Bun-side consumers (the API and the cluster harness) connect to the same socket path with Bun.listen/Bun.connect. I still call this "IPC" throughout - IPC means inter-process communication, and a Unix socket is one mechanism for that, in the same family as pipes or shared memory.

sentences.en: One terminology note: the transport under all of this is a Unix domain socket, not TCP.
sentences.zh: 一个术语说明：所有这些下的传输是 Unix 域套接字，而不是 TCP。

sentences.en: Go listens with net.Listen("unix", ...); the Bun-side consumers (the API and the cluster harness) connect to the same socket path with Bun.listen/Bun.connect.
sentences.zh: Go 使用 net.Listen("unix", ...); 进行监听Bun 端消费者（API 和集群线束）使用 Bun.listen/Bun.connect 连接到相同的套接字路径。

sentences.en: I still call this "IPC" throughout - IPC means inter-process communication, and a Unix socket is one mechanism for that, in the same family as pipes or shared memory.
sentences.zh: 我仍然将其称为“IPC”——IPC 意味着进程间通信，Unix 套接字是一种机制，与管道或共享内存属于同一家族。

blocks.html_en: Zero-downtime deploys: generations

sentences.en: Zero-downtime deploys: generations
sentences.zh: 零停机部署：几代人

blocks.html_en: The old deploy path used PM2, and PM2's restart (not reload) meant the whole bot process - manager included - went down and came back up. That's a real "gap" in gateway connections on every deploy. The naive fix, a plain reload instead of a restart, has its own failure mode: for a moment you'd have old and new code both attached and both handling the same events, i.e. duplicate event handling.

sentences.en: The old deploy path used PM2, and PM2's restart (not reload) meant the whole bot process - manager included - went down and came back up.
sentences.zh: 旧的部署路径使用 PM2，PM2 的重新启动（而不是重新加载）意味着整个机器人进程（包括管理器）出现故障并重新启动。

sentences.en: That's a real "gap" in gateway connections on every deploy.
sentences.zh: 这是每次部署时网关连接中真正的“差距”。

sentences.en: The naive fix, a plain reload instead of a restart, has its own failure mode: for a moment you'd have old and new code both attached and both handling the same events, i.e. duplicate event handling.
sentences.zh: 天真的修复，简单的重新加载而不是重新启动，有它自己的失败模式：一会儿你会同时附加旧的和新的代码，并且都处理相同的事件，即重复的事件处理。

blocks.html_en: The fix I came up with is generation-tagged shard ranges. Each deploy spins up a new "generation" of clusters holding the same shard ranges as the old generation, in parallel. The manager waits for the new generation to report ready before it flips routing over to it. Only after the flip happens does it tell the old generation to quiesce - stop accepting new work, finish in flight, then exit.

sentences.en: The fix I came up with is generation-tagged shard ranges.
sentences.zh: 我提出的修复方法是使用代标记的分片范围。

sentences.en: Each deploy spins up a new "generation" of clusters holding the same shard ranges as the old generation, in parallel.
sentences.zh: 每次部署都会并行地启动新一代集群，这些集群拥有与旧一代相同的分片范围。

sentences.en: The manager waits for the new generation to report ready before it flips routing over to it.
sentences.zh: 管理器等待新一代报告准备就绪，然后再将路由切换到它。

sentences.en: Only after the flip happens does it tell the old generation to quiesce - stop accepting new work, finish in flight, then exit.
sentences.zh: 只有在翻转发生之后，它才会告诉老一代停止——停止接受新工作，完成飞行，然后退出。

blocks.html_en: The ordering is the whole point: routing flips between "new generation ready" and "old generation quiesced", never before the new one's ready (the event listeners might not be loaded, DB connection might be missing, etc.) and never long after the old one's quiesced (you'd have a gap). That ordering guarantees there's no window where a guild's events could route to two generations at once, and no window where they route to none.

sentences.en: The ordering is the whole point: routing flips between "new generation ready" and "old generation quiesced", never before the new one's ready (the event listeners might not be loaded, DB connection might be missing, etc.) and never long after the old one's quiesced (you'd have a gap).
sentences.zh: 顺序就是重点：路由在“新一代就绪”和“旧代停顿”之间切换，永远不会在新代准备好之前（事件侦听器可能未加载，数据库连接可能丢失等），也不会在旧代停顿之后很久（你会有一个间隙）。

sentences.en: That ordering guarantees there's no window where a guild's events could route to two generations at once, and no window where they route to none.
sentences.zh: 这种顺序保证了公会的事件不会同时传递给两代人，也不会传递给任何人。

blocks.html_en: I considered simpler options - a full restart, or just accepting the old downtime (even though it was just a few seconds) - and rejected them because at SupportMail's scale, a full-restart gap means dropped gateway events across every guild simultaneously, not a cosmetic blip. Rolling per-cluster deploys with a bounded quiesce window costs more implementation complexity but limits the actual "damage" to something measurable and small.

sentences.en: I considered simpler options - a full restart, or just accepting the old downtime (even though it was just a few seconds) - and rejected them because at SupportMail's scale, a full-restart gap means dropped gateway events across every guild simultaneously, not a cosmetic blip.
sentences.zh: 我考虑了更简单的选项 - 完全重启，或者只是接受旧的停机时间（即使只是几秒钟） - 并拒绝了它们，因为在 SupportMail 的规模下，完全重启间隙意味着同时删除每个公会的网关事件，而不是表面现象。

sentences.en: Rolling per-cluster deploys with a bounded quiesce window costs more implementation complexity but limits the actual "damage" to something measurable and small.
sentences.zh: 使用有限的静止窗口滚动每个集群的部署会增加实施的复杂性，但将实际的“损害”限制在可测量的和较小的范围内。

blocks.html_en: What's better now: deploys roll out cluster-by-cluster instead of all-at-once, the quiesce gap is bounded and observable instead of open-ended, and there's no duplicate-event-handling window to worry about - versus the old world, where a deploy was closer to "hope nothing important happens in that gap."

sentences.en: What's better now: deploys roll out cluster-by-cluster instead of all-at-once, the quiesce gap is bounded and observable instead of open-ended, and there's no duplicate-event-handling window to worry about - versus the old world, where a deploy was closer to "hope nothing important happens in that gap."
sentences.zh: 现在更好的是：部署是逐个集群推出而不是一次性推出，静默间隙是有界的且可观察的而不是开放式的，并且无需担心重复事件处理窗口 - 与旧世界相比，部署更接近于“希望在该间隙中没有发生任何重要的事情”。

blocks.html_en: Splitting the HTTP API out

sentences.en: Splitting the HTTP API out
sentences.zh: 拆分 HTTP API

blocks.html_en: The old client-api depended directly on bot internals and lived attached to the manager process - deploying the API meant touching the same process tree as the bot.

content_html_zh:
SupportMail 是一个 Discord 机器人 - 具体来说是 modmail - 管理如此多的用户，以至于它无法再生活在单个网关连接中。 与该规模的每个机器人一样，它必须进行分片：将其服务器拆分为多个连接，并且在超过某个点后，拆分为多个进程。 长期以来，该机器都是一个独立的 Node/Bun 扩展库，围绕机器人生成和管理集群子进程。 在过去的几周里，我用 Go 编写的专用主管、重写的集群工具以及机器人的 REST API 和机器人本身之间的适当划分来替换它。

这篇文章是关于重写的：为什么旧的设置不理想，我构建了什么，以及现在实际上更好的东西。

注意：开发人员用于“Discord 服务器”的术语是“公会”。

分片到底是什么，SupportMail 之前有什么

如果您不深入了解 Discord 机器人的内部结构，您可能听说过“分片”这个词，但不需要知道它的含义。 值得解释一下，因为本文的其余部分都依赖于此。

分片是与 Discord 的一个网关连接，负责一部分公会。 Discord 不允许您将机器人所在的每个公会放在单个 WebSocket 连接上 - 超过一定大小，一个连接将无法跟上事件量，Discord 通过要求您在机器人超过公会计数阈值时进行分片来强制执行此操作。 哪个公会属于哪个分片不是任意的：它是 (guildId >> 22)%totalShards，一个确定性哈希，因此系统的任何部分都可以弄清楚哪个分片拥有给定的公会，而无需询问任何人。

这是最简单的部分。 更困难的部分是“更多分片”不是免费的 - 您不能只从一个进程打开 500 个网关连接并称其为完成。 分片被分组为集群，其中每个集群都是一个单独的进程，包含少量分片。 当你有多个进程时，你需要在它们之上的东西来决定要运行多少个集群，哪些分片进入哪个集群，重新启动一个死亡的集群，并为外部世界（API，仪表板）提供一个地方来询问“公会 X 的分片现在是否还活着”。 那东西就是主管。

SupportMail 的旧主管是 gactic.ts，它是另一个机器人的分片管理器，使用节点的 child_process 模块。 我的它的分支使用 Bun.spawn() 从 StandaloneInstance 中分支出集群子进程，所有子进程都位于同一个 Bun 进程中，该进程还在端口 3000 上运行机器人的 REST API，并在端口 4000 上运行 WebSocket 服务器。 一切——网关连接、HTTP、套接字、管理程序逻辑本身——都是一棵 Bun 进程树。

如果“为什么分片”没有落地，那么接下来的几个部分也不会落地 - 将结构操作与业务操作分开，基于代的部署，同样的想法。 仍然只有多个进程和一个协调器，只是规模较小。

为什么要替换它而不是修补它

开始整个重写的具体痛苦是：Bun.spawn、child_process 和机器人进程内部使用的工作线程破坏了 Sentry 检测。 主要工序还是包子。 通过节点的diagnostics_channel发布的错误事件根本不起作用，并且在集群子节点参与时就默默地丢失了。 这是一个“我不能相信我自己的错误报告”错误。

仅此一点并不能真正修补，因为 Bun 的发布时间表很奇怪，而且开放 PR 似乎并没有很快合并 - 最新的 Bun 版本也是两个多月前发布的，并且没有新版本发布的迹象。 让它不值得修补的是它下面的东西：gactic.ts 的 Instance/Cluster 类与父进程是 Bun 的假设相耦合。 选择是将其修补到位并保持 Bun 本地化，或者完全放弃它并以不同的语言进行外部处理。 两者之间没有什么。 一旦你回顾了 gactic.ts 本身，它所管理的大部分内容一开始就不难理解：discord.js 已经原生支持一个进程中的多个分片（内部分片）——gactic.ts 处理的是围绕它的编排，而不是分片本身。

公平地说，旧代码 - 无需停机的重新集群逻辑、进程之间的 IPC 通信以及我在 fork 中添加的清理并不是自重。 它们对于我最终构建的生成/静止切换来说是有用的参考材料——值得保留的部件被保留作为参考，结构上不合适的部件被替换。

考虑的替代方案

上面的部分介绍了为什么无法在适当的位置修补 gactic.ts。 即使抛开这一点，留在进程中也不是正确的选择：SupportMail 不是我运行的唯一机器人 - 我还有 Ticketon，有一天它可能需要相同的基础设施 - 并且连接到一个机器人进程的管理器如果不进行另一次重写就无法重复使用。 这就是由外部的、与机器人无关的主管以不同的语言解决的问题。

说到语言，这仍然是开放的。 我最初考虑 Rust，主要是因为我想要一个借口来更多地了解它。 然而我选择了 Go，原因有两个：

  1. 并发模型直接适合问题的形状。 “监督 N 个集群进程并通过套接字扇入它们的 IPC”几乎正是 goroutine 和通道的用途。 Rust 的异步故事 - 选择运行时、Pin、发送/同步边界线程贯穿所有内容，这会带来复杂性来解决 Go 用几行代码即可解决的问题。
  2. 建设速度。 Go 的标准库（net、exec、net/http）足以构建管理器、IPC 集线器和状态 WebSocket，几乎没有第三方依赖项。 Rust 意味着选择和学习异步运行时，并在编写任何实际的主管逻辑之前拿起箱子。

这并不意味着 Rust 更糟糕。 这是一个“运输目标与学习目标”的计算，对于如此接近生产关键的基础设施，运输获胜。

核心设计决策：结构操作与业务操作

这就是核心路由设计。

管理器（sm-manager）仅理解五种操作：REGISTER、HEARTBEAT、QUIESCE、QUIESCED 和 DEPLOY。 这些是结构性的 - 它们与流程生命周期有关，而不是与机器人的行为有关。 流经管理器的其他所有内容都是不透明的字符串，由目标寻址，管理器将其路由到正确的集群，而无需查看其内部。

为什么这很重要：管理器从不解析业务负载。 它不知道“关闭票证”操作是什么样子，或者“同步行会配置”操作，或者机器人关心的任何其他东西 - 它只知道将其发送到哪里。 这意味着经理完全与机器人无关。 让第二个机器人使用相同的基础设施，只需使用不同的配置文件就意味着我们不必分叉管理器代码库。 （具体来说，这可以让 Ticketon 共享 sm-manager，而经理无需知道 Ticketon 的存在。）

另一种选择——一个理解每项操作的管理者——已经隐式地摆在了桌面上，因为这基本上就是单一主管的样子。 它的耦合性更强：每一个需要跨集群协调的新机器人功能/功能更改都意味着管理器代码更改，并且管理器在实践中永远只有一个机器人，即使理论上没有什么可以阻止您转向第二个机器人。

粗略地说，路由看起来像这样：

client → sm-manager:
  { op: "DEPLOY", ... }         → structural, manager handles directly
  { op: "guild.sync", target: clusterId, payload: <opaque> }
                                → business, manager forwards untouched to target

管理器根据 op 是否是五个结构代码之一进行分支。 如果是，它就会起作用。 如果不是，它会查看目标，找到所属的集群连接，然后转发整个消息负载。

零停机部署：几代人

旧的部署路径使用 PM2，PM2 的重新启动（而不是重新加载）意味着整个机器人进程（包括管理器）出现故障并重新启动。 这是每次部署时网关连接中真正的“差距”。 天真的修复，简单的重新加载而不是重新启动，有它自己的失败模式：一会儿你会同时附加旧的和新的代码，并且都处理相同的事件，即重复的事件处理。

我提出的修复方法是使用代标记的分片范围。 每次部署都会并行地启动新一代集群，这些集群拥有与旧一代相同的分片范围。 管理器等待新一代报告准备就绪，然后再将路由切换到它。 只有在翻转发生之后，它才会告诉老一代停止——停止接受新工作，完成飞行，然后退出。

顺序就是重点：路由在“新一代就绪”和“旧代停顿”之间切换，永远不会在新代准备好之前（事件侦听器可能未加载，数据库连接可能丢失等），也不会在旧代停顿之后很久（你会有一个间隙）。 这种顺序保证了公会的事件不会同时传递给两代人，也不会传递给任何人。

我考虑了更简单的选项 - 完全重启，或者只是接受旧的停机时间（即使只是几秒钟） - 并拒绝了它们，因为在 SupportMail 的规模下，完全重启间隙意味着同时删除每个公会的网关事件，而不是表面现象。 使用有限的静止窗口滚动每个集群的部署会增加实施的复杂性，但将实际的“损害”限制在可测量的和较小的范围内。

现在更好的是：部署是逐个集群推出而不是一次性推出，静默间隙是有界的且可观察的而不是开放式的，并且无需担心重复事件处理窗口 - 与旧世界相比，部署更接近于“希望在该间隙中没有发生任何重要的事情”。

拆分 HTTP API

旧的客户端 API 直接依赖于机器人内部结构，并附加到管理器进程 - 部署 API 意味着与机器人接触相同的进程树。

我决定也将其外包 - sm-api 通过与任何其他客户端使用的完全相同的 Unix 套接字协议与 sm-manager 通信来修复该问题 - 没有特殊的访问路径，没有通过机器人内部的快捷方式。 它只是另一个 IPC 客户端。

回报是 sm-api 独立于机器人重新部署。 而且由于它经历了上述相同的结构/业务运营拆分，因此它永远不会回到依赖机器人内部形状的位置。 但它与机器人流程分离的事实也是一个好处。

可观察性作为证明点

结构/业务分离的另一个地方在实践中得到了回报：公共状态页面 WebSocket 位于 sm-manager 上，而不是机器人上。 心跳有效负载基本上逐字转发给它，这对管理器来说是不透明的，就像任何其他业务有效负载一样。

这证实了这种分割在它设计的情况之外仍然有效——管理器不需要特殊的情况来支持公共状态提要，因为“转发不透明的有效负载而不理解它”已经是默认行为。

现在有什么好

  • 哨兵仪器有效 - 开始重写的最初原因。
  • 部署几乎是零停机时间，具有有限且可测量的停顿窗口，而不是“无论重新启动需要多长时间”。
  • 管理器与机器人无关：第二个机器人是配置添加，而不是管理器分支。
  • 该 API 与机器人进程完全解耦 - 没有共享进程树，没有内部形状依赖性。
  • 它正在生产中 - 自切换以来，SupportMail 一直在其上运行。 这不是标题，但切换后内存使用量下降了大约 40%。
  • 管理器和 API 现在都是 systemd 服务，而不是 pm2 管理的，因此它们会在主机重新启动时自动返回，而不需要进程管理器来照顾它们。

闭幕式

有些事情仍然被故意推迟。 传输是 Unix 套接字，而不是 TCP 或 WebSocket，目前这很好，因为一切都在一台主机上运行 - 但如果情况发生变化，这将是一个限制。 管理器还没有高可用性故事；它是一个单一进程，如果它死掉了，系统会重新启动它，而不是由热备接管。 如今，这两个问题都不是问题，也不需要在第一天就解决，因为理论上存在差距。 我真的很难找到“但是如果”和“现在真的需要吗”之间的界限。

sm-manager 可能最终会在某个时候开源，因为它与机器人无关并且不是特定于 SupportMail 的。 我无法给出日期 - 我将更新这篇文章，并在发生这种情况时单独发布一篇新文章。
